newsitem.title: USA: Dry Kansas wheat areas have chance for rain.
newsitem.headline: Dry Kansas wheat areas have chance for rain.

text.p: Dry hard red winter wheat areas in western Kansas may receive scattered showers next week, but the long-term outlook for that area remains dry, meteorologists said.

"The outlook is not great," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, regarding rain in western Kansas. He said a cool front to arrive late Sunday may produce scattered showers followed by a second rain system Tuesday and Wednesday.
"I'm not confident it is going to produce meaningful moisture," he said.

During the first half of May, rainfall in Garden City in southwest Kansas was eight percent of normal at 0.8 inch and in Goodland in northwest Kansas it was 0.27 inch or 19 percent of normal. April rainfall in Garden City was 64 percent of normal and Goodland's was 58 percent, said Burgio.

Craig Solberg, Freese-Notis Weather meteorologist, estimated these areas could receive rain amounts of 0.3 to 0.7 inch next week, as well as above normal temperatures in the 80s and low 90s degrees Fahrenheit.
